svg.title: How each flight metric is measured on a step response
svg.desc: Two responses to the same commanded step. The underdamped response rises past the goal; its overshoot is the largest excursion beyond the goal after the first crossing, and its settling time is when it last enters and stays inside the plus or minus five centimetre band. The overdamped response never crosses the goal, so its overshoot is zero by definition while it still has a settling time. Root mean square error is computed across the whole segment, not at a single instant.
svg.text: Overshoot. The largest excursion beyond the goal after the first crossing. If the response never crosses the goal,
overshoot is zero. Report it as zero rather than measuring the closest approach.
Settling time. The time after which the response enters the ±0.05 m band and stays there. A brief re-exit resets it.
RMS error. Computed across the whole segment, not at one instant, so a response that is close on average scores better,
and a fast but oscillatory flight can score worse than a slower, smoother one.
